anchor.quote: Let $p$ be the number of fractional binary places kept, so the grid spacing is $2^{-p}$.
Let $z$ be a finite list of complex numbers, called coefficients.
Then $Q_p z$ is the list obtained by truncating each real and imaginary part of each coefficient toward zero to the grid $2^{-p}\mathbb{Z}$.
Truncation to precision $p$ is built from the [Integer](integer.md) $\mathbb{Z}$, the set of integers, because its grid $2^{-p}\mathbb{Z}$ consists of the multiples of $2^{-p}$.
The error of truncation is measured by the [Array norm](array-norm.md) $\|\cdot\|_\infty$, the largest complex modulus of any coefficient.
